findings.blocking_reason: Wrong-language UI text is a quality/correctness issue but does not break build, security, data, or API contracts.
findings.body: The `totpStep1` key in the Lithuanian (`_lt`) properties file was replaced with Italian text: `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. This is not Lithuanian — it is a copy-paste error from an Italian translation. The surrounding keys (`totpStep2`, `totpStep3`) are correctly in Lithuanian, which confirms this is an accidental wrong-language insertion. Lithuanian users will see a mixed-language string in the TOTP setup screen. The same pattern (replacing the old anchor-tag-containing string with a localized generic sentence) was applied to fi/sk/sv correctly, but lt received the wrong source text.
findings.evidence: git show HEAD on messages_lt.properties shows the file as fully added (153 insertions); line 101 reads `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` while lines 102-103 (`totpStep2`, `totpStep3`) are in Lithuanian (`Atidarykite programėlę...`, `Įveskite programėlėje...`).
findings.suggestion: Replace the value with a proper Lithuanian translation, e.g. `totpStep1=Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`
findings.title: Italian text introduced into Lithuanian translation file

findings.blocking_reason: This is a regression: the Lithuanian translation was correct before this PR and is now replaced with Italian text shown to end users during MFA enrollment.
findings.body: The `loginTotpStep1` key in the Lithuanian translation bundle was replaced with **Italian** text instead of Lithuanian. The new value is `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:"), not Lithuanian. The surrounding entries (`loginTotpStep2`, `loginTotpStep3` on lines 72-73) remain in proper Lithuanian (`Atidarykite programėlę...`, `Įveskite programėlėje...`), confirming this is an isolated copy-paste error — not a wholesale locale swap. The original Lithuanian value was `Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje. Programėlės prieinamos Google Play ir Apple App Store.` — proper Lithuanian with anchor links. The PR's sanitizer-driven update was supposed to remove the anchors and rephrase to match the English reference (`Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`), but the Lithuanian translation was replaced with Italian text instead. For comparison, the actual Italian bundle (`messages_it.properties:92`) has `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo dispositivo mobile` — nearly identical but with `dispositivo mobile` instead of `cellulare`, indicating this is not even a clean copy from the Italian bundle but likely a translation-tool mishap. **Impact**: Lithuanian users setting up TOTP will see Italian text in the FreeOTP setup instructions. This is a user-facing regression in a security-critical flow (MFA enrollment).
findings.dimension_name: Coverage Gap 5 - cluster_10 community login messages (21 locales)
findings.evidence: Step 1: PR diff for messages_lt.properties shows `loginTotpStep1` changed from `Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje...` to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Step 2: Reading the actual file themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties line 71 confirms: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Step 3: `grep -in 'installa\|applicazioni\|cellulare\|seguenti' messages_lt.properties` returns only line 71 — no other Italian text in the file. Step 4: Surrounding lines 72-73 (`loginTotpStep2`, `loginTotpStep3`) are in proper Lithuanian, confirming isolated copy-paste error. Step 5: English reference (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties:128) is `loginTotpStep1=Install one of the following applications on your mobile:` — the Lithuanian should be a Lithuanian translation of this, not Italian. Step 6: This file is rendered in the FreeOTP/TOTP setup flow shown to end users during MFA enrollment — a user-facing security-critical screen.
findings.suggestion: Replace line 71 with a proper Lithuanian translation, e.g. `loginTotpStep1=Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame įrenginyje:` to match the English reference intent. The translator should verify the Lithuanian phrasing; the key point is the value must be in Lithuanian, not Italian.
findings.title: Italian text substituted for Lithuanian translation in messages_lt.properties

findings.blocking_reason: Logic imperfection in a theme-verification utility causes confusing diagnostics, but does not break the build, tests, or any production runtime behavior.
findings.body: The `santizeAnchors` loop `break`s on the first anchor that doesn't match the English source. If a translation contains three anchors and the second one is modified, the third anchor is never inspected nor stripped — so an illegal third anchor silently passes through to the HTML sanitizer, which may then emit a confusing diff message rather than the precise `Didn't find anchor tag` diagnostic. Worse, the method only removes anchors that match exactly; a non-matching anchor is reported but left in `value`, which then gets sanitized downstream — the reported message and the actual sanitized output can disagree. The loop should continue after reporting a mismatch (or collect all mismatches) rather than aborting.
findings.evidence: Lines 156-159: `} else { messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"); break; }` — the break exits the while loop on first non-match.
findings.suggestion: Replace `break;` with `continue;` (or collect mismatches and continue), and decide explicitly whether to strip non-matching anchors from `value` before returning it to the sanitizer.
findings.title: santizeAnchors breaks on first mismatch, skipping remaining anchors and their verifications

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test coverage for an untested happy path is non-blocking per the bar.
findings.body:
The test suite contains 4 tests, all asserting that violations are **detected** (`verifyDuplicateKeysDetected`, `verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`). There is **no test** that verifies a valid German translation (with HTML that matches the English reference, or with no HTML when English has none) produces an empty `messages` list.

This is a fundamental coverage gap: a regression in `verifySafeHtml()`, `santizeAnchors()`, or `normalizeValue()` that causes **false positives** (flagging all valid translations as illegal) would not be caught by any existing test. For a build-time tool that gates ~40 translation files, a false-positive regression would block the build silently.

The most important untested happy path is `santizeAnchors()` when anchors match exactly: the method removes matching anchors via `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` while the `Matcher` continues scanning the original string. This fragile pattern (modifying `value` while iterating via a `Matcher` bound to the old string) has no test coverage for the case where it should succeed.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `verifyValidTranslationPasses` does not exist in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java` (lines 30-52 show only 4 violation-detection tests).
Step 2: `santizeAnchors()` (VerifyMessageProperties.java:150-162) has two branches: (a) anchors match → `value.replaceFirst(...)` removes anchor, continues; (b) anchors don't match → adds error message, breaks.
Step 3: Only branch (b) is tested via `changedAnchor_de.properties` (malicious.com vs example.com href).
Step 4: Branch (a) — the common real-world case where translations preserve anchor tags — has zero test coverage. A regression in `replaceFirst` logic or `Matcher` state would be undetected.
findings.suggestion:
Add a test case `verifyValidTranslationPasses()` with a fixture pair (e.g., `validAnchor_de.properties` / `validAnchor_en.properties`) where the German translation contains the same anchor as English plus only allowed HTML (``, `

`, `
`, ``). Assert `verify()` returns an empty list. Also add a test where English has no HTML and German has no HTML — assert empty list.
findings.title: No positive test case verifying that valid translations pass without errors

findings.blocking_reason: Inconsistent exception type propagation is a code quality issue that produces a less clean error message, but does not break the build, cause data loss, or constitute a regression of previously working behavior.
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` wraps IOExceptions in `RuntimeException` (lines 70 and 79), but the caller `verify()` catches `IOException` and throws `MojoExecutionException`. Because `verifySafeHtml` is called inside the `try { ... } catch (IOException e) { throw new MojoExecutionException(...) }` block on lines 48-54, the thrown `RuntimeException` is NOT caught by the `catch (IOException)` clause — it propagates up uncaught and crashes the Maven plugin with a raw stack trace instead of a clean MojoExecutionException. This breaks the plugin's error-handling contract and produces a poor user experience (unstructured exception rather than `Can not read file ...`).
findings.evidence: Line 70: `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + file, e);` — the enclosing try/catch on lines 48-54 only catches `IOException`, so this RuntimeException bypasses the MojoExecutionException conversion.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) have `verifySafeHtml` declare `throws IOException` and let the existing catch in `verify()` wrap it, or (b) catch the RuntimeException in `verify()` and re-throw as `MojoExecutionException`. Option (a) is simpler and matches the existing `verifyNoDuplicateKeys` pattern.
findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException while verify() contract declares MojoExecutionException — inconsistent error propagation

findings.blocking_reason: Wrong-language translation content is a localization quality issue with no demonstrated security exploit path or contract break.
findings.body: The totpStep1 message key (TOTP authenticator setup instruction shown to users enabling 2FA) has multiple translations containing content in the wrong language or wrong variant, indicating a systemic localization QA control gap rather than isolated typos. Lithuanian (messages_lt.properties:101) contains Italian text `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Simplified Chinese (messages_zh_CN.properties:112) contains Traditional Chinese characters `手機/應用程式/安裝` instead of Simplified `手机/应用程序/安装`. Separately each might be dismissed as a one-off copy-paste error; together they expose a pattern where translation files for the same key were never reviewed for language correctness. Notably the Italian text in lt does not even match the current messages_it.properties value (`...sul tuo dispositivo mobile`), and the zh_CN text does not match the current zh_TW value (`在您的手機中安裝下列程式 (擇一)`), suggesting stale/wrong sources were pasted and never validated. Because this string instructs users during TOTP enrollment — a security-sensitive flow — wrong-language instructions can cause users to misunderstand the setup step or abandon 2FA enrollment. An individual reviewer catching only one occurrence could treat it as a trivial typo; the repeated pattern across unrelated language pairs (Romance language misplaced into Baltic; Traditional variant misplaced into Simplified) reveals the absence of a verification step that should catch wrong-language content across the whole translation set.
findings.evidence: messages_lt.properties:101 `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian, not Lithuanian); messages_zh_CN.properties:112 `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` (Traditional characters 手機/應用程式/安裝, not Simplified 手机/应用程序/安装); base en:150 `totpStep1=Install one of the following applications on your mobile:`; current it:138 `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo dispositivo mobile` (differs from lt's Italian text); current zh_TW:150 `totpStep1=在您的手機中安裝下列程式 (擇一)` (differs from zh_CN's Traditional text); messages_lv.properties has no totpStep1 key at all (falls back to English).
findings.suggestion: Run a localization QA pass over ALL totpStep* keys in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_*.properties: (1) replace lt totpStep1 with a correct Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile'; (2) replace zh_CN totpStep1 with Simplified Chinese `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`; (3) add the missing totpStep1 key to messages_lv.properties; (4) add a CI/script check that flags translation values whose Unicode script/variant does not match the locale (e.g., CJK variant detector, Romance-language detector for non-Romance locales) to prevent recurrence.
findings.title: Systemic wrong-language content in totpStep1 translations across account theme

findings.blocking_reason: This describes a latent completeness gap in a verification utility tool, not a production code path break, security exploit, data loss, API contract break, or behavioral regression.
findings.body:
The two contributing findings describe the same code mechanism (normalizeValue line 124-126) from different angles. Together they reveal a systemic control gap that neither captures alone:

1. KEY-GATED WHITELIST: The choice-format stripping on line 124-126 only runs for two specific key prefixes: `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`. Any future message key using MessageFormat choice syntax with the `<` operator (e.g. `1<values`, `4<hodnôt` — both patterns already exist in the repo) will NOT have its choice format stripped.

2. SANITIZE/UNESCAPE ROUNDTRIP SILENTLY SWALLOWS THE `<`: When a non-whitelisted key's choice format is not stripped, the `<` character survives into the HTML sanitization step. The OWASP sanitizer with POLICY_NO_HTML escapes `<` to `<`, but line 95 immediately calls `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized)`, which turns `<` back to `<`. The resulting `sanitized` string equals the original `value`, so `Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` (line 99) returns true and NO error is raised. The `<` passes through the entire roundtrip unchanged — the HTML check is silently bypassed.

3. FRAGILE REGEX: Even for whitelisted keys, the regex `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` (line 126) stops at the first `}`. Any future choice format containing nested braces would not be fully stripped, leaving `<` and `}` characters in the value.

COMBINED: The verifier's protection depends on (a) maintaining an exhaustive, undocumented whitelist of keys with choice formats and (b) the choice format never containing `}`. Both assumptions are implicit. An individual reviewer seeing either finding alone might dismiss it as 'latent' or 'works by accident.' Together they show the verification mechanism is fundamentally keyed to specific known strings rather than a general rule — any future MessageFormat choice usage outside the whitelist silently evades the HTML sanitization check, giving a false sense of security. Existing Slovak (messages_sk.properties:501) and Czech (messages_cs.properties:501) translations already use 4-option choice formats with `4<` (`{1,choice,0#hodnôt|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnôt}`), confirming the `<`-in-choice-pattern is an established convention that could appear in new keys.
findings.evidence:
Line 124: `else if (key.startsWith("linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit") || key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size"))` — whitelist gate restricting stripping to two key families.
Line 126: `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");` — `[^}]*` stops at first `}`, latent nested-brace fragility.
Line 95: `sanitized = org.apache.commons.text.StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(sanitized);` — unescape reverses the sanitizer's `<`→`<` escaping.
Line 99: `if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value))` — comparison passes (no error raised) when `<` survives the sanitize→unescape roundtrip.
messages_sk.properties:501: `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Atribút {0} musí mať najmenej {1} {1,choice,0#hodnôt|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnôt} a najviac {2} {2,choice,0#hodnôt|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnôt}.` — real 4-option choice format with `4<` operator.
messages_cs.properties:501: similar 4-option pattern with `4<hodnot`.
findings.suggestion: Replace the key-gated whitelist with a general MessageFormat placeholder stripper that runs for ALL keys before sanitization, e.g. `value = value.replaceAll("\\{\\d+(?:,\\w+(?:,[^{}]*)?)?\\}", "...")` to strip all MessageFormat placeholders (including choice formats) regardless of key. Additionally, do NOT call `unescapeHtml4` on the sanitized output (line 95) — or if quote-entity unescaping is needed, unescape only `'`/`"` rather than all HTML4 entities, so that `<`/`>` escaping from the sanitizer is preserved and the comparison on line 99 actually detects unescaped `<` that survived normalizeValue. Add a comment documenting why choice-format `<` must be stripped before sanitization.
findings.title: Key-gated choice-format whitelist + fragile regex + sanitize/unescape roundtrip = silent HTML-check bypass for future choice-format keys

findings.blocking_reason: Brittle string replacement for locale suffixes is a code quality/robustness concern with no demonstrated regression or security vulnerability.
findings.body: The English reference bundle is located by `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. Two issues: (1) The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` uses a character class that includes `-` and `_`, which is fine, but it will also match files like `messages_en_US.properties` correctly — however, if a locale contains a digit (rare but possible in BCP-47 variants like `es_419`), it will NOT match and the English file lookup will fail with a confusing RuntimeException. (2) The `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` assumes a specific directory naming convention; if the community theme is ever restructured or the verifier is run against a non-community theme, the lookup silently points to the wrong file or throws. There is no validation that `englishFile` actually exists before constructing the bundle.
findings.evidence: Lines 74-75: two chained `replaceAll` calls with no existence check on the resulting path.
findings.suggestion: Use `java.nio.file.Path` to derive the sibling English file: resolve the filename by replacing only the locale suffix using a strict regex like `_(?:[a-z]{2,3}(?:_[A-Z]{2})?(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\.properties$` → `_en.properties`, and verify the path exists with `Files.exists()` before loading — emit a clear `MojoExecutionException` if missing.
findings.title: English reference file path derived via brittle string replacement — fragile against locale suffixes and path layouts

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a hypothetical future key that doesn't exist yet; current behavior works for existing keys with no demonstrated production impact.
findings.body: The newly introduced English source string `error-invalid-multivalued-size` uses `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The `normalizeValue` special-case regex `\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` requires the inner content to contain no `}` character, which is fine here, but `[^}]*` also stops at the first `}` — and choice formats never contain `}` internally so this works by accident. The real problem is that `1<values` contains a `<` that the regex does NOT strip because the `<` is inside the choice body and the whole token is replaced with `...` — but only when the key is `error-invalid-multivalued-size` OR starts with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`. If a future key uses `<` inside a choice format, it will silently break. The whitelist is brittle and undocumented.
findings.evidence: Line 126: `value = value.replaceAll("\\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}", "...");` — key-gated on line 124.
findings.suggestion: Generalize: strip all `{...}` MessageFormat placeholders (including choice formats) with `value.replaceAll("\\{[^{}]*}", "...")` before sanitizing, rather than key-specific special-casing.
findings.title: Choice-format regex `{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}` does not match the actual `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` pattern in messages_en.properties

findings.blocking_reason: The finding is speculative about potential double-evaluation and does not concretely demonstrate build breakage, contract breakage, or production regression; the reviewer acknowledges the change is likely a correct fix and merely asks for verification and tests.
findings.body: The English source string changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. Two concerns: (1) `{{0}}` in the original was a literal-escaped placeholder that rendered as `{0}` — changing it to `{0}` means it now gets substituted with the attribute name. This is likely the intended fix (the original was probably a bug that showed `{0}` literally), but any downstream consumer (e.g. the admin UI React layer) that was compensating for the double-brace will now double-substitute. (2) The choice format `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is appended outside the sentence structure — for `values=0` it reads `... at most 0 values` (correct) but the pluralization does not agree with the earlier `value(s)` that was removed. The change is correct in intent but should be verified against the rendering layer to confirm `{0}` is actually substituted and not double-escaped.
findings.evidence: Diff: `-error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` → `+error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`
findings.suggestion: Verify in the admin UI that the rendered string shows the actual attribute name (not `{0}`) and that the choice-format pluralization renders correctly for counts 0, 1, and 2+ in English. Add a unit or integration test that exercises the rendered message for all three counts.
findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder format changed from `{{0}}` to `{0}` — potential double-evaluation and consumer breakage

findings.blocking_reason: Code style and encapsulation suggestion with no demonstrated correctness, security, or production impact.
findings.body: `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, `POLICY_NO_HTML`, and `HTML_TAGS` are declared as instance fields without `private` or `final`. They are effectively immutable constants (the `PolicyFactory` is built once and never reassigned, and `Pattern` is thread-safe immutable). They should be `private static final` to (a) prevent accidental reassignment, (b) clarify intent that these are constants shared across all instances, and (c) follow Java naming conventions for constants. `ANCHOR_PATTERN` on line 145 is correctly declared `private static final` — the others should match.
findings.evidence: Line 58: `PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = new org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder()` — no modifier. Compare line 145: `private static final Pattern ANCHOR_PATTERN = ...`.
findings.suggestion: Change to `private static final PolicyFactory POLICY_SOME_HTML = ...;`, `private static final PolicyFactory POLICY_NO_HTML = ...;`, and `private static final Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile(...);`.
findings.title: Constants POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML, HTML_TAGS are non-final non-private instance fields

findings.blocking_reason: Missing tests for edge cases is explicitly non-blocking per the release bar.
findings.body:
The `normalizeValue()` method in `VerifyMessageProperties.java` (lines 117-137) has 4 special-case branches that strip legitimate `<` / `>` characters from specific keys before HTML sanitization:

1. `templateHelp` — strips `CLAIM.<NAME>` patterns
2. `optimizeLookupHelp` — strips `<Extensions>`
3. `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` — strips `{0,choice,...}` format strings

None of these keys appear in any test fixture. A regression in these regex patterns (e.g., a pattern that over-strips and masks an XSS payload, or under-strips and produces false positives on valid translations) would be invisible to the test suite. These special cases exist precisely because the sanitization logic would otherwise flag legitimate content — they are security-critical exceptions that need regression tests.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `normalizeValue()` (VerifyMessageProperties.java:117-137) has 4 conditional branches keyed on specific property names.
Step 2: No test fixture in `src/test/resources/` contains keys named `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, or `error-invalid-multivalued-size` (verified via glob of 6 fixture files).
Step 3: These branches modify `value` before OWASP sanitization — if the regex is wrong, either false positives (blocking valid translations) or false negatives (missing XSS) occur.
Step 4: No test exercises these branches → regression risk is unmitigated.
findings.suggestion: Add test fixtures that include keys `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` with their respective special patterns. Verify both directions: (a) valid patterns pass without errors, (b) actual XSS in these keys is still detected (the regex doesn't over-strip).

findings.blocking_reason: Missing reverse completeness check in a theme verification tool is a code-quality/functional-improvement suggestion, not a build break, security vulnerability, data loss, API break, or regression.
findings.body: The `santizeAnchors()` method iterates only over **translation** anchors via `while (matcher.find())` and calls `englishMatcher.find()` in tandem. If the translation has **fewer** `` tags than the English source, the loop simply terminates earlier — the missing English anchors are never detected. **Scenario:** English has `Documentation Security Policy` (2 anchors), translation has only `Documentation` (1 anchor, matching). The loop iterates once, the match succeeds, the anchor is removed from `value`, and the method returns. The second English anchor (Security Policy link) is silently dropped from the translation with no error reported. **Security assessment:** This is NOT a phishing/href-injection gap — no malicious content is introduced. A translator cannot inject a malicious URL through this path because extra anchors with different hrefs would be caught by the exact-string comparison (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`), and the OWASP sanitizer (`POLICY_SOME_HTML` which does NOT allow `a` elements) strips any remaining `` tags as a backstop. However, it IS a functional/integrity gap: a translator could silently remove required links (documentation, terms of service, security policy) from localized messages, degrading the user experience for non-English users. The method's Javadoc states: "Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key." This is a one-directional check (translation anchors ⊆ English anchors) with no reverse check (English anchors ⊆ translation anchors).
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `santizeAnchors()` is called at line 88 with `value` (translation) and `englishValue` (English source).
Step 2: Line 151 creates `matcher` from translation `value`; line 152 creates `englishMatcher` from `englishValue`.
Step 3: Line 153 `while (matcher.find())` iterates ONLY over translation anchors. If translation has 1 anchor and English has 2, the loop runs once.
Step 4: Line 154 `englishMatcher.find()` advances the English matcher in lockstep. After the loop, `englishMatcher` has only consumed 1 of 2 English anchors.
Step 5: No post-loop check verifies `englishMatcher` is exhausted. Method returns at line 161 with no error.
Step 6: The missing English anchor is never reported.

Test coverage gap: `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java` has `verifyNoChangedAnchors` (tests href swap → caught) but no test for missing/fewer anchors scenario.
findings.title: Missing anchor tags in translation go undetected — no reverse completeness check

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test for an edge case is explicitly non-blocking per the bar.
findings.body:
When the English reference file cannot be found, `verifySafeHtml()` throws `RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile)` (VerifyMessageProperties.java:79). This is an unchecked exception that propagates through `verify()` (which only catches `IOException` and wraps it in `MojoExecutionException`) to the caller.

The test suite does not verify this behavior. There is no test case that:
1. Points to a translation file whose corresponding `_en.properties` file does not exist
2. Asserts that a `RuntimeException` (or specific error message) is thrown

While the error-handling pattern itself (RuntimeException vs MojoExecutionException) is being reviewed in a parallel dimension, the **test coverage gap** belongs here: without a test, a change to the error handling (e.g., gracefully skipping missing English files, or wrapping in MojoExecutionException) could break without detection.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `verifySafeHtml()` (VerifyMessageProperties.java:76-80) opens `englishFile` via `FileInputStream` and catches `IOException` → throws `RuntimeException`.
Step 2: `verify()` (line 46-56) catches `IOException` → wraps in `MojoExecutionException`. RuntimeException is NOT caught.
Step 3: No test in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java` (lines 30-52) uses a fixture without a corresponding `_en.properties` file.
Step 4: Every test fixture has either a self-referencing `_en` file (illegalHtmlTag_en, duplicateKeys_en) or a paired `_en` file (noHtml_en, changedAnchor_en). Missing-reference path is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a test `verifyMissingEnglishReferenceFileThrows()` that creates a fixture with a locale suffix (e.g., `orphan_de.properties`) with no corresponding `orphan_en.properties`, and asserts the expected exception type and message. This locks down the contract regardless of whether the team decides RuntimeException or MojoExecutionException is correct.
findings.title: No test for behavior when English reference file does not exist (RuntimeException propagation)

findings.blocking_reason: This is a code quality/error-reporting improvement with no security, correctness, or production impact, as the sanitizer backstop still catches any remaining mismatched anchors.
findings.body:
When `santizeAnchors()` encounters a mismatched anchor (either the English matcher is exhausted or the anchor strings don't match), it executes `break` at line 158, exiting the while loop. Any remaining translation anchors in `value` are not checked by the anchor validator.

**Security assessment:** This is NOT a security gap. The downstream OWASP sanitizer (`policy.sanitize(value)` at line 92) uses `POLICY_SOME_HTML` which allows only `br, p, strong, b` — **not** `a`. Any `<a>` tags remaining in `value` after the break are stripped by the sanitizer. The comparison `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` at line 99 then detects the difference and reports "Illegal HTML in key...". So href-injection through extra/mismatched anchors is prevented by defense-in-depth.

**Quality gap:** The developer sees two different error messages for the same class of problem: "Didn't find anchor tag X in original string" (from `santizeAnchors` for the first mismatch) and "Illegal HTML in key...: '<a href=...>' vs. ''" (from the sanitizer for subsequent anchors). This makes debugging harder when a translation has multiple modified anchors — the developer must fix one, re-run, then see the next. Continuing the loop instead of breaking would report all mismatched anchors in one pass.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: Translation has 3 anchors: anchor1 (matches English), anchor2 (mismatched href), anchor3 (mismatched href).
Step 2: Iteration 1: matcher finds anchor1, englishMatcher finds English anchor1, `Objects.equals` → true, removed from value.
Step 3: Iteration 2: matcher finds anchor2, englishMatcher finds English anchor2, `Objects.equals` → false. Line 157: message "Didn't find anchor tag anchor2 in original string". Line 158: `break`.
Step 4: anchor3 is never checked by santizeAnchors. It remains in `value`.
Step 5: Line 92 `policy.sanitize(value)` strips anchor3 (since `a` is not in POLICY_SOME_HTML allowlist).
Step 6: Line 99 `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` → true. Line 111: message "Illegal HTML in key...: '<a href=...>' vs. ''".
Step 7: Developer sees two different error formats for the same root cause (modified anchors), requiring two fix-and-iterate cycles.
findings.title: break on first mismatch stops checking remaining anchors — degraded error reporting quality

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test coverage for whitelist edge cases is a non-blocking test-quality gap, not a build, correctness, or security regression.
findings.body: The PR introduces a key-specific whitelist in `normalizeValue` that strips `<NAME>`-style placeholders and MessageFormat choice tokens for four key families. None of the four new test methods (`verifyDuplicateKeysDetected`, `verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) exercise these special cases. If a future refactor accidentally removes a whitelist branch, the build will still pass but real translations will start failing with false-positive `Illegal HTML` reports. The whitelist is the most fragile part of this change and has the least test coverage.
findings.evidence: Test methods on lines 31-46 only cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML tag, no HTML, and changed anchors — none reference the whitelisted keys.
findings.suggestion: Add a test fixture pair (e.g. `placeholders_de.properties` / `placeholders_en.properties`) that includes `templateHelp` with `CLAIM.<NAME>`, `optimizeLookupHelp` with `<Extensions>`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` with a choice format, and assert that `verify()` returns no `Illegal HTML` messages for them.
findings.title: No test covers the key-specific whitelist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter, error-invalid-multivalued-size)
